assumptions: The proposed service remains an administrative matching, exception-handling, and evidence workflow; it does not take certificate inventory or conduct proprietary commodity trading.
An authorized TGE registry participant can legally and contractually perform transfers and cancellations for the service on commercially workable terms, although no such commitment is evidenced.
The initial beachhead is Polish brokers, advisers, and multi-site buyers with genuinely difficult allocation or claims-proof exceptions, rather than every Guarantee-of-Origin transaction.

The founder can use contractors or advisers for energy-law, registry, and environmental-claims matters while retaining product and data-system ownership and remaining within the stated part-time limit.
The reported Polish GO volume is a directional market denominator, not evidence that an equivalent share is addressable or that transaction volume converts into attractive service revenue.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid, end-to-end pilot with an authorized registry partner and several multi-site accounts showing recurring hard exceptions, documented baseline versus product time and error reduction, claim-safe accepted outputs, actual onboarding and usage prices, partner take rate, gross margin after exception labor, acquisition cost, payback, renewal intent, and a credible volume path that does not require a large share of the Polish market.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The concept correctly anchors value to a registry-confirmed cancellation matched to a site and reporting period, where unique ownership, temporal and market boundaries, and claims wording matter. That is sharper than selling a generic sustainability report, but the insight is not exclusive: TGE and incumbent platforms already support much of the transfer, allocation, cancellation, and proof workflow.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Reporting deadlines, certificate expiry, double-counting controls, and UOKiK claims risk create a credible recurring problem with potentially costly errors. The packet does not establish how often target buyers face hard allocation exceptions, what those exceptions currently cost, or whether brokers or buyers will pay separately rather than expect the work from their existing energy provider.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A fee on confirmed work, no speculative inventory, modest stated startup capital, and software-assisted matching could produce good cash conversion. However, price, gross margin, partner fees, exception-review labor, CAC, payback, retention, and founder time are all unknown; the proposed route also gives an authorized broker substantial bargaining power, while the founder-net-worth case depends on reaching 4 TWh, about 7.5% of the cited Polish reference volume.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish GO activity is large enough to support a focused service, and multi-site entities or broker books with complicated allocations form a reasonably narrow initial segment. Yet the packet does not quantify the number of exception-heavy accounts, their service spend, or the portion not already served, and the year-six volume ambition is too large to function as a conservative beachhead case.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Direct evidence shows TGE reducing batching and discovery friction and Ecohz, Soldera, and Energy Solution already providing substantial parts of the proposed workflow. A Polish white-label exception layer could occupy a niche, but there is no exclusive registry access, committed channel, or demonstrated capability that would let it dominate even that niche before incumbents or partners reproduce it.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A trusted allocation ledger could extend into additional entities, reporting periods, certificate types, evidence controls, or nearby geographies. Cross-border recognition and connectivity remain unresolved, however, and broader procurement and multi-country workflows move the company directly toward established platforms with deeper coverage.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Integrations, historical exception resolutions, customer-specific allocation rules, and audit continuity could create some switching cost and learning effects after scale. The proposed operator does not initially control registry access or distribution, incumbents can accumulate similar data, and no proprietary data right, exclusive partnership, network effect, or regulatory authorization moat is evidenced.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Claim-safe proof packets and careful site-period matching could improve trust and exception handling, but the packet provides no measured improvement in cost, speed, accuracy, or liability relative to incumbent broker and platform workflows. TGE bulk functions and incumbent dashboards weaken any convenience advantage based mainly on orchestration.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Digitized GO transactions, formal Scope 2 quality criteria, residual-mix accounting, and recent scrutiny of certificate-backed claims increase the value of accurate evidence and wording. At the same time, TGE's 2026 bulk and marketplace functions show that infrastructure is improving in ways that compress the simplest service layer, so timing favors a compliance-exception product more than a generic retirement desk.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Brokers and PPA advisers are concentrated routes to relevant buyers and could support white-label scale without a founder-led personal brand. No channel commitment or conversion evidence exists, installers may not reach the procurement or reporting owner, and the best channels are also capable providers that control customer access and may prefer to internalize the workflow.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The structured-data workflow, renewable-energy adjacency, controlled initial capital, and AI leverage fit the founder reasonably well. Delivery still depends on registry authorization, highly accurate allocation, legal boundaries, claims controls, partner cooperation, and potentially manual exception review; a double claim or misleading proof packet could create disproportionate liability, and part-time operating load has not been tested.

highest_value_structural_change: Recast the business as a broker-embedded exception and claims-control product: the authorized broker retains registry, trading, and client responsibility; the company owns the allocation-policy engine, exception benchmark corpus, and claim-safe evidence controls; and the broker pays an annual minimum platform fee plus usage fees for resolved exceptions. Start with one committed broker's existing multi-site book, making recurring software revenue depend on difficult cases solved rather than on capturing several TWh of commodity volume.
main_structural_strength: The service ties payment to a verifiable registry event and can remain capital-light by separating auditable allocation and exception handling from certificate inventory and trading.
primary_score_limiter: The necessary registry and distribution partners already control the customer and can perform or copy much of the workflow, leaving the operator without a proven advantage, protected control point, or demonstrated margin capture.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: TGE added bulk transactions and a marketplace in April 2026, while Ecohz, Soldera, and Energy Solution already offer procurement, allocation, cancellation, status monitoring, proof storage, or Polish TGE certificate delivery; this directly contradicts a broad orchestration-gap thesis.
